name: Breadcrumbs
purpose: Show a user's location in a nested/hierarchical section via an ordered trail of ancestor links ending in the current page.
intent: Provide a consistent, accessible 'you are here' trail composed from the existing Link atom, rather than every page reinventing separators and spacing.

figmaSource.note: A single component (not a variant set) showing 8 repeated breadcrumb-item instances - no size/tone axis to capture.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 8-item demo renders every crumb - including the last - as an identical Link instance with no distinct 'current page' treatment. The component deliberately renders the last item in `items` as non-interactive text with aria-current="page" instead, per the WAI-ARIA Breadcrumb Pattern - documented here as an intentional adaptation, not a literal 1:1 reproduction.
Whether an item is 'current' is derived from the absence of `href`, not a separate isCurrent flag - simplest possible rule, consistent with Link's own required `href`.
iconBefore/iconAfter are exposed as arbitrary ReactNode, matching the BOOLEAN toggle properties Figma exposes on the breadcrumb-item part.

The current-page item no longer uses --color-content-default to visually distinguish it from ancestor links - per explicit design feedback, that differentiation wasn't wanted; it now uses the same --color-content-subtle as Link's own appearance=subtle, so every item in the trail reads at the same visual weight.

Link's own :visited treatment (a real browser-history-driven purple color swap) is intentionally overridden back to Link's normal resting/press color for every breadcrumb ancestor - per explicit design feedback, 'have you visited this URL before' isn't a signal breadcrumbs should surface, since it makes the trail read as a list of arbitrary hyperlinks rather than a location path. This is a documented, deliberate exception to the 'do not restyle Link's own hover/focus/press treatment' compositionRule below - it targets :visited specifically, not those states.

useCases: any page needing a location trail back to ancestor levels
antiPatterns: primary navigation for a shallow/single-level app
linear flow progress with unvisited future steps
more than one trail per page

anatomy.description: One per entry in `items`, in order.
A literal '/' character before every item except the first.
Rendered for every item that has an href.
Rendered for the item without an href - always the last item in practice.

items.description: Ordered list of trail entries, root first, current page last.

ariaLabel.description: Accessible name for the nav landmark.

className.description: Optional custom class name for the root nav.

label.description: The visible text/content for this level.

href.description: Presence makes the item a Link; absence marks it as the current page.

iconBefore.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

iconAfter.description: Optional icon rendered after the label.

onClick.description: Forwarded to Link; only applicable to non-current items.

slots.name: items[].iconBefore / items[].iconAfter
supports: a small icon from the generated icon set

color.link: inherited from Link appearance=subtle, with :visited overridden back to the resting/press color (see compositionRules)

requirements: nav must always have an accessible name (aria-label, default 'Breadcrumb').
The current (last, href-less) item must carry aria-current="page".
Do not add role=list/listitem manually - ol/li already carry the correct implicit roles.

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves through each ancestor Link in order; the current item is not focusable.
behaviorRules: Render items in the given order, one li per item.
Render a '/' separator before every item except the first.
Render an item with href as the Link atom (appearance=subtle, size=md).
Render an item without href as non-interactive text with aria-current="page".
Render iconBefore/iconAfter around the label when provided.
compositionRules: Breadcrumbs always renders Link for ancestor items - do not restyle or reimplement Link's own hover/focus/press treatment locally.

The one documented exception: Breadcrumbs overrides Link's :visited color back to its normal resting/press color, via a higher-specificity selector scoped to .item .link (no !important) - a visited-URL signal doesn't belong in a location trail. Hover/focus/press remain entirely Link's own.
Use Progress Indicator instead of Breadcrumbs for step-based flow progress.
contentRules: Keep labels short - no truncation or wrapping is built in.
The last item in `items` should not have an href.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all color comes from semantic tokens (Link's own tokens, plus --color-content-default/--color-content-subtle).
implementationNotes: Use React.memo for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, or typography.
Reuse the Link atom directly for every ancestor item rather than reimplementing anchor styling.
do: Use for a real hierarchical location trail.
Omit href on the current (last) item so it renders as aria-current text.
dont: Do not use for shallow/single-level navigation.
Do not use for linear flow progress with unvisited steps.
Do not add href to the current/last item unless it should actually be a link.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders one li per item, in order.
No separator before the first item; a separator before every subsequent item.
Items with href render as Link.
The item without href renders as non-interactive text with aria-current="page".
nav has an accessible name, defaulting to 'Breadcrumb'.
Uses --spacing-sm between items and --spacing-xs between an icon and its label.
Tests cover ordering, separator placement, link vs current rendering, icons, ariaLabel, and className.
knownLimitations: No truncation, wrapping, or collapsed/overflow behavior for long trails or narrow containers.
futureEnhancements: A collapsed/overflow variant (e.g. 'Home / ... / Security') for long trails
